summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual customer-facing assistant. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; key criteria: context length for long conversations, multilingual support (EN/JA/ES), tool-calling to internal APIs, and security (SOC2/KMS/VPC). Agreed next steps: send model matrix, schedule dedicated pilot, share compliance docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-06-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Arielle (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dana (Head of ML, Celestia), Omar (Platform Eng), Lina (SecOps), Marcus (PM)

[00:00] Arielle (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Arielle, I'll run the call, and Marco from our SE team will handle the deeper model/perf questions. Happy to go around real quick for intros?

[00:10] Dana (Celestia): Dana, Head of ML at Celestia Systems. We're building a multi-lingual customer assistant that needs long conversational context and ability to call internal APIs for order lookups.

[00:18] Omar (Celestia): Omar, platform engineer, will own deployment and networking questions.

[00:22] Lina (Celestia): Lina, security and compliance. I'll be looking at SOC2, KMS integration, VPC options.

[00:28] Marcus (Celestia): Marcus, PM for the assistant product. Focused on user flows and latency targets.

[00:35] Arielle: Great. Quick agenda — understand model selection needs (context length, multilingual, tool-calling), talk about hosting options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), and align on next steps. Sound good?

[00:44] Dana: Yep. We're evaluating open models primarily — cost matters, but we can't sacrifice quality for warranty, especially for Japanese and Spanish. Also some enterprise constraints might push us to Dedicated or Private.

[00:55] Marco (Redwood SE): Cool. Can you share your main success metrics? P95 latency target, tokens per request, max convo length?

[01:04] Dana: p95 we want under 700ms for short queries, but for long context flows 1.2-1.5s is acceptable. Average user conversation ~20 turns, but we want to support 10k+ token context for certain workflows — knowledge-heavy threads where users paste docs. Multilingual: English, Japanese, Spanish. Must support tool-calls to our internal order and billing API with structured JSON responses.

[01:40] Marco: Okay — model-wise that points toward variants with longer context windows (16k, 32k, 100k). Open models like Llama-3-family, Mistral-instruct-ish, and some of the long-context open models could be candidates. We usually recommend testing 32k and 100k context variants for the paste-doc use case.

[01:58] Arielle: Just to clarify on hosting, Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and managed SLAs; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation (reserved GPU pools); Private gives full network isolation and on-prem options. For SOC2 + KMS you can do Hosted with customer-managed KMS or Dedicated/Private. Lina, is customer-managed KMS required or just preferred?

[02:20] Lina: Prefer customer-managed KMS for key separation, and VPC peering required for any sensitive PII traffic. SOC2 docs are a must.

[02:28] Arielle: Understood — we can share SOC2 + network diagrams.

[02:34] Omar: For Dedicated pilot, what infra footprint would we need? We're running in GCP and have specific VPC restrictions.

[02:42] Marco: For a 2-week Dedicated benchmark with mixed short/long requests, typical test config is 4 A100-equivalent GPUs for initial throughput testing, with autoscale thresholds. We'll provide a pilot plan that includes simulated traffic and end-to-end latency numbers. We can also do a Hosted benchmark first if you want faster turnaround, though throughput won't be reserved.

[03:05] Dana: We prefer Dedicated for predictable unit economics, but we need to compare cost. Also want to ensure model parity between Hosted and Dedicated — if we train/finetune or use different quantizations, results should be consistent.

[03:18] Marco: Model parity is something we aim for — same model weights and inference kernels where possible. Quantization/acceleration differences can cause small deltas; we provide quantization profiles and recommended prompts for evals.

[03:30] Arielle: Let's dig into model candidates quickly. Any model owners we should be aware of? Are you leaning open-only?

[03:36] Dana: Open-first, but if a closed model gives marked quality wins in Japanese we might consider it. Still prefer open due to cost and control.

[03:45] Marco: For open models, we often test Llama-3 variants (with 32k and 64k contexts), Mistral large for instruction tasks, and Falcon-180B-instruct-style clones for certain tasks. There are also long-context specialized models (we mentioned some on our model catalog). Important: tool-calling/structured outputs — some model decoders handle function-like responses better; we instrument outputs with two layers: prompt templates + small response validators.

[04:10] Marcus (PM): For tool-calling, latency on round-trip to our APIs matters. We will want streaming responses and partial function call options so UI feels snappy.

[04:20] Marco: Redwood supports streaming and function/tool calling primitives — function call payloads can be passed to your backend, and we support structured JSON responses. We also have fallbacks so if tool call fails we can still respond with a human-readable message.

[04:33] Lina: From security, we need audit logs for all calls and RBAC for who can trigger private endpoints. Also retention policies — we cannot keep PII logs for more than 30 days.

[04:44] Arielle: We can configure retention and per-customer retention windows. Audit logs are included; we can include token-level tracing masked for PII.

[04:54] Omar: Network-wise, can Redwood Dedicated be peered into our VPC in GCP? We'd prefer that over routing via the public internet.

[05:02] Marco: Yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private modes include on-prem. For Hosted, we offer VPC egress options and customer-managed KMS for encrypting logs at rest. There are some onboarding steps for firewall rules. We'll include a network diagram in the follow-up.

[05:18] Dana: On multilingual quality — do you have benchmarks for Japanese and Spanish across the open models?

[05:24] Marco: We have curated eval sets for several languages; results vary. Rough guidance: Llama-3 and certain instruction-tuned Mistral variants do well in Japanese; Falcon-family models can drop in non-English. We'll include our matrix with Rouge/BLEU-ish metrics and human eval notes. Also recommend you run your representative prompts because domain-specific terms can trip models.

[05:48] Arielle: How about context/window handling for 100k tokens? Any gotchas?

[05:54] Marco: The main tradeoffs are memory and latency. For long contexts we leverage KV cache management and prefix caching to reduce repeated compute. Some models degrade in quality when you push to extreme lengths — we recommend retrieval-augmented snippets + chunking for very large docs rather than feeding 100k raw tokens every request. But for your use-case (paste-heavy knowledge threads) a 32k–100k variant with good chunking and caching is reasonable.

[06:25] Dana: That makes sense. We do a lot of document search + context assembly, so maybe retrieval + 32k is sufficient. We'll still want an option for larger contexts for power users.

[06:34] Marcus: On cost — can you share ballpark per-1k-token pricing across Hosted vs Dedicated reserved pricing?

[06:40] Arielle: We'll send a pricing matrix. Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated has committed monthly cost plus lower per-token inference unit economics. We'll put numbers in the matrix and model-specific compute multipliers so you can compare.

[06:54] Lina: Regarding compliance, please send SOC2 report and a sample contract redline for data residency. Also we need to validate KMS flow — who holds the keys for Hosted when we request customer-managed KMS?

[07:06] Marco: For customer-managed KMS, your key material remains in your cloud KMS and we integrate via encryption at rest keys; we can provide a whitepaper and sequence diagram. For Private on-prem you hold everything locally.

[07:18] Arielle: Okay let's capture next steps. We'll send model comparison, pricing, SOC2 and network docs. Marco will draft the Dedicated pilot plan. Dana, you'll share sample prompts/dataset.

[07:30] Dana: Sounds good. Also, can we get a quick demo showing tool-calling flow with our API shape?

[07:35] Marco: Yes — we can demo function-calling mapping with your JSON schema. We'll need a short schema and an example endpoint.

[07:42] Arielle: Any other blockers?

[07:45] Omar: Nothing immediate. We'll need a security questionnaire later but that's standard.

[07:49] Lina: We'll likely run a short security review after the pilot.

[07:52] Arielle: Great — recap of action items in the chat and via email. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the matrix and pilot plan.

[07:58] Dana: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
